research_scope: Five full formulation reviews: finite linear rank, module linearity, kernel preimage and two degree constructions. Ten unassigned references plus one contextual correction.

amendments.review_rationale: Read rank of K-linear transformation with finite-dimensional image as dimension of image subspace, explicitly finite nonnegative integer and separate from nullity.
amendments.reason: Read the complete mathematical formulation and effective reference set; classify current unassigned concepts and correct the mapping/preimage context without disturbing prior annotations.

references.context: Linear algebra: image of a K-linear transformation as a subspace of target W admitting a finite K-basis.
references.reason: Finite-dimensional vector subspace is reusable independently of finite rank.

references.context: Linear algebra: dimension dim_K U of a finite-dimensional K-vector space U is the finite cardinality of any K-basis of U.
references.reason: Dimension is reusable; finite rank of T is the dimension of the image.

references.disposition: Definition does not assign a finite integer rank to infinite-dimensional image.

amendments.review_rationale: Read additive and scalar-preserving R-linear map between left modules over same associative ring, without requiring the ring to be a field.
amendments.reason: Read the complete mathematical formulation and effective reference set; classify current unassigned concepts and correct the mapping/preimage context without disturbing prior annotations.

references.matching_note: The source assumes an associative ring but does not require a specified multiplicative identity or unital module action. Use the general left-module meaning rather than the stricter unital convention.

references.disposition: The equality T(m+m′)=T(m)+T(m′) is the additive axiom defining module linearity.
The equality T(rm)=rT(m) is the scalar axiom defining module linearity.
This variant allows general associative rings and is not limited to vector-space transformations.
references.phrase: module linearity does not assume field K

amendments.review_rationale: Read kernel of K-linear transformation as inverse image of zero vector in W, an additive subspace of source V rather than target W.
amendments.reason: Read the complete mathematical formulation and effective reference set; classify current unassigned concepts and correct the mapping/preimage context without disturbing prior annotations.

references.phrase: vector spaces V,W over common field

references.context: Set theory: inverse image f^{-1}(B)={x∈X:f(x)∈B} of a subset B⊆Y under f:X→Y; here B={0_W}.
references.reason: Preimage is a reusable set construction distinct from a mapping itself or from its kernel.

references.disposition: Zero is the additive identity already supplied by the target vector-space structure.
The set of vectors mapped to zero is exactly the kernel being defined; recursive self-linking would be circular.
The preimage uses target zero but is a subset of source V.

amendments.review_rationale: Read degree of vertex in simple undirected graph by count of incident edges, preserving cardinality interpretation for potentially infinite graphs.
amendments.reason: Read the complete mathematical formulation and effective reference set; classify current unassigned concepts and correct the mapping/preimage context without disturbing prior annotations.

references.context: Graph theory: an undirected edge e is incident with v when v is one of the edge's endpoints.
references.reason: Edge-vertex incidence is a reusable relation independent of counting the incident edges.

references.phrase: cardinality of set of incident edges
references.matching_note: The number/cardinality of incident edges is the set-theoretic cardinality of this edge subset.

references.disposition: The graph is simple and loopless, so each edge contributes at most one to degree of v.

amendments.review_rationale: Read simple graph vertex degree as cardinality of adjacent distinct neighbors and its coincidence with edge incidence in loopless graph.
amendments.reason: Read the complete mathematical formulation and effective reference set; classify current unassigned concepts and correct the mapping/preimage context without disturbing prior annotations.

references.context: Graph theory: neighborhood N_G(v)={u∈V:{u,v}∈E} in a simple undirected graph G=(V,E).
references.reason: Vertex neighborhood is a reusable graph construction distinct from vertex degree.

references.matching_note: The number of distinct neighboring vertices is the cardinality of the neighborhood.

references.phrase: degree counts neighbors only for simple graph
references.disposition: For multigraph with parallel edges, degree based on neighbor count can differ from incident-edge count.
